subject: Implementing Tests from Kolenikov and Bollen (2012)

messages.author: 8fad79f76b1ae521
messages.subject: Implementing Tests from Kolenikov and Bollen (2012)
parts:
Apologies in advance if this is a cross-posting as I could not find a clear answer to my question. In modeling some of my data, I have come upon the "negative variances" error (e.g. Heywood cases) for one of the variables that I am including, whose variance is generally only a tad bit under 0 (e.g., -.039). This variable does have some skew/kurtosis but it is not egregious, and I have cleaned the data for outliers. I have seen the 2012 article by Kolenikov and Bollen referenced multiple times so I decided to read it to make sure that I am systematically examining the potential causes for the negative variance. Though I understand the general gist of what the tests are exploring compared to the null hypotheses, I am not proficient enough to follow all of the mathematics and derivations hence I am having difficulty understanding how to actually implement the bootstrapped tests around the variance in lavaan. I read through the lavaan manual and tutorial to find the bootstrapLavaan() function but cannot seem to make it work.

Are there more specifics about implementing the bootstrapped tests from Kolenikov and Bollen (2012) in Lavaan or perhaps another solution in R that I have missed by focusing on Lavaan? Please let me know if any other information is helpful/needed - I am new to both R and SEM.

Thank you!

Reference
Kolenikov, S., & Bollen, K. A. (2012). Testing Negative Error Variances: Is a Heywood Case a Symptom of Misspecification? Sociological Methods & Research, 41(1), 124–167. https://doi.org/10.1177/0049124112442138

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Implementing Tests from Kolenikov and Bollen (2012)
parts: I read through the lavaan manual and tutorial to find the bootstrapLavaan() function but cannot seem to make it work.

You can just request bootstrapped SEs when you fit the model with se="boot" and boot=2000 or so (see ?lavOptions), then request a bootstrap CI from parameterEstimates().

But you should be fine with the CI using robust SEs, e.g., estimator = "MLR", which you can view in summary(fit, ci=TRUE).
